description: The Danish shore-based AIS system, owned by the Danish Maritime Authority under the EU vessel traffic monitoring directive (2002/59/EC), collects the Automatic Identification System messages of ships in Danish waters: ship identification (name, call sign, IMO and MMSI numbers), navigation (position, course and speed) and voyage data (destination, arrival time and draught). Class A transponders are compulsory for ships over 300 gross tonnage, passenger ships and fishing vessels over 15 m, and smaller craft may carry class B. Coverage is national, the Danish waters. Historical AIS data are free to download as zipped CSV files that are continuously updated, while web access and online data flows are sold as annual subscriptions under the authority's data management policy; the land-based system is now under the Danish Emergency Management Agency. Data are held in the real-time system for up to 24 months, and older data are packed and offered as open data for a limited period. Caveats: AIS comes from ships' own instruments and can contain errors, class B and non-equipped vessels are under-represented, and users need their own tools to handle the files. The data support traffic density, collision and grounding risk, port capacity and disruption studies, and the DMA also publishes passage lines and transit routes. They complement the US Marine Cadastre AIS data.
